answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a separate $100 bond for 30 days before receiving a daily job quota. Whether agents sell glacier forecasts or quill illustrations, no bond can back two identities at once. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up $100,000 for a month, plus fees and lost investment returns. This makes the market a poor haven for cheap sybil swarms: extra identities require extra capital.
